open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A name is judged when the folder is observed.
open_points.question: At which exact event is a folder name observed: directory-entry enumeration, metadata read, file open, or completion of the scan, and must that one observation govern all later checks in the operation?
options: Judge the name when its directory entry is enumerated.
Judge the name immediately before metadata or content is read.
Revalidate the name at every check and use the latest name.
open_points.default_guess: Judge the name once when its directory entry is enumerated and retain that observed path for the operation.

witness.initial: An ordinary file is present under a name that is not ignored.
events: The deliverer enumerates the parent folder.
Syncthing renames the file to a name containing `.sync-conflict-` before the deliverer reads its metadata or opens it.
outcomes: The enumeration is the observation, so the ordinary name was accepted and the vanished observed path is reported as `unreadable_file`.
The metadata/open step is the observation, so the new conflict-copy name is ignored and no observation is reported.
witness.observer: The calling flow reading the scan result.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent`
open_points.question: Must this failure occur only when the content has no existing placement, or does it also override the rule that placed content replays when only a conflict copy holds it?
options: Fail only when no placement already exists; otherwise replay the existing placement.
Fail whenever the only current file is a conflict copy, even if a placement already exists.
open_points.default_guess: Replay an existing placement without reading the conflict copy; use `not_ready_or_absent` only when a new placement would be required.

witness.initial: A source hash already has a placement, and the only remaining file with that content has a conflict-copy name.
events: The calling flow requests placement using that source hash.
outcomes: The normative rule and the later Required tests phrase require replay of the existing placement.
witness.observer: The calling flow receiving the placement outcome.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed
open_points.question: When an ordinary file and a conflict copy have identical content and therefore the same hash, does placement by that hash succeed through the ordinary file or fail because a conflict copy also has the hash?
options: Succeed using the observed ordinary file and disregard the conflict copy.
Fail whenever any conflict copy has the requested hash.
Define an explicit precedence rule for selecting an eligible observed path.
open_points.default_guess: Succeed using the ordinary observed path; an ignored conflict copy must not make otherwise eligible content unavailable.

witness.initial: An ordinary file and a conflict copy contain identical bytes and no placement exists for their shared hash.
events: A scan reports the ordinary file and ignores the conflict copy.
The calling flow requests placement by the shared hash.
outcomes: The conflict-copy test phrase says placement by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent`.
The ordinary-file test phrase and normative rule say the ordinary file is placed.
witness.observer: The calling flow receiving success or failure.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: a file renamed to a conflict copy after the observation fails with `unreadable_file` and writes nothing
open_points.question: Does this renamed-file failure apply when the content already has a placement, or does replay take precedence without reading the renamed file?
options: Replay takes precedence whenever a placement exists.
The result depends on whether the placement was found before or after path revalidation.
open_points.default_guess: Look up and replay an existing placement before attempting to read or revalidate a source path.

witness.initial: An ordinary file is observed and its content already has a placement.
events: After observation, the file is renamed to a conflict-copy name.
The calling flow requests placement using its source hash.
outcomes: The renamed-file Required tests phrase requires `unreadable_file`.
The normative replay rule requires the existing placement to be returned whatever name the content has now.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed
open_points.question: What must the INV-18 test show to prove that the conflict copy was not the source of the new placement when the ordinary file has identical content?
options: Assert that the placement records the ordinary observed path and instrument or arrange the files so opening the conflict path is detectable.
Assert only that placement succeeds, without proving which path supplied the bytes.
Remove or alter the conflict copy after the scan so a successful placement demonstrates that the ordinary path was used.
open_points.default_guess: Require the test to make access to the conflict-copy path detectable and assert that only the ordinary observed path supplies the placement.

witness.initial: An ordinary file and a conflict copy contain identical bytes.
events: The implementation chooses one of the two paths as the source of a new placement.
The required test asserts only that the content is placed.
outcomes: An implementation reads the ordinary file and satisfies INV-18.
An implementation reads the ignored conflict copy and produces the same stored bytes, so the stated assertion passes while INV-18 is violated.
witness.observer: The invariant test or reviewer, which cannot distinguish the implementations from the required assertion.
